root_cause.text: The `check_imm` macro in the arm64 BPF JIT compiler uses an off-by-one error in its bit-shift validation, checking for an (N+1)-bit signed range instead of the actual N-bit signed range required by ARM64 branch instruction encodings, allowing out-of-range immediates to pass validation and be silently truncated by the encoder.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the shift amount from `(bits)` to `((bits) - 1)` in both the positive and negative range checks. The CVE description explicitly states that the original macro "admits values in [-2^N, 2^N)" when it should only admit "[-2^(N-1), 2^(N-1))", and demonstrates the concrete impact: "for check_imm19(), values in [2^18, 2^19) slip past the check but do not fit into the 19-bit signed imm19 field of B.cond. aarch64_insn_encode_immediate() then masks the raw value into the 19-bit field, setting bit 18 (the sign bit) and flipping a forward branch into a backward one."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix immediate value range validation in BPF JIT by adjusting bit shift offset to correctly check signed immediate bounds.
intent_record.what: Modified the check_imm macro to subtract 1 from the 'bits' parameter in both bit shift operations: changed '(imm) >> (bits)' to '(imm) >> ((bits) - 1)' and '~(imm) >> (bits)' to '~(imm) >> ((bits) - 1)'.
intent_record.how: This changes the bit range validation logic for immediate values. Previously, the macro checked if an immediate value exceeded the range of 'bits' bits. Now it checks against 'bits - 1' bits, effectively reducing the valid range by one bit position. This makes the validation stricter, rejecting immediate values that would have previously been accepted.

grouping_result.intent: Fix immediate value range validation in BPF JIT by adjusting bit shift offset to correctly check signed immediate bounds.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the off-by-one error in immediate value range validation by adjusting the bit shift offset in the check_imm macro. This fix corrects the signed immediate bounds checking to match the actual N-bit signed range required by ARM64 branch instructions, which is the core issue described in the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This line checks if a positive immediate is out of range by right-shifting by `bits` positions. However, for an N-bit signed range, the check should shift by (bits-1) to properly validate the signed bounds. Shifting by `bits` instead of `bits-1` creates an off-by-one error that allows values requiring N+1 bits to pass validation when only N bits are available.

This line checks if a negative immediate is out of range by right-shifting the bitwise complement by `bits` positions. Similar to the positive case, this should use (bits-1) to correctly validate the N-bit signed range. The off-by-one error allows negative values outside the valid N-bit signed range to pass validation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs an off-by-one error in validating positive immediate values. It checks if a positive immediate is out of range by right-shifting by `bits` positions, but for an N-bit signed range, it should shift by (bits-1). This allows values requiring N+1 bits to incorrectly pass validation when only N bits are available in the ARM64 branch instruction encoding.

This statement performs the same off-by-one error for negative immediate values. It checks if a negative immediate is out of range by right-shifting the bitwise complement by `bits` positions, but should use (bits-1) to correctly validate the N-bit signed range. This allows negative values outside the valid N-bit signed range to pass validation and be silently truncated by the encoder.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the `check_imm` macro at lines 30-39 with the vulnerable off-by-one error in bit-shift validation. The macro checks `(((imm) > 0) && ((imm) >> (bits)))` for positive values and `(((imm) < 0) && (~(imm) >> (bits)))` for negative values. This checks for an (N+1)-bit signed range instead of the actual N-bit signed range. For example, with bits=19, it should validate the range [-2^18, 2^18-1] but instead validates [-2^19, 2^19-1]. The macro is then used in `check_imm19(jmp_offset)` and `check_imm26(imm)` calls throughout the newly added `emit_ll_sc_atomic()` function (lines 113, 125, 137, 149) without any correction. The vulnerable construct is clearly present and the fix (correcting the bit-shift logic to properly validate N-bit signed ranges) is not applied in this commit.

Author: Zi Shen Lim <zlim.lnx@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Aug 26 21:15:30 2014 -0700

    arm64: eBPF JIT compiler
    
    The JIT compiler emits A64 instructions. It supports eBPF only.
    Legacy BPF is supported thanks to conversion by BPF core.
    
    JIT is enabled in the same way as for other architectures:
    
            echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/core/bpf_jit_enable
    
    Or for additional compiler output:
    
            echo 2 > /proc/sys
bic_trace_step.reason: The `check_imm` macro at lines 397-404 contains the off-by-one error described in the vulnerability. The macro checks `if ((((imm) > 0) && ((imm) >> (bits))) || (((imm) < 0) && (~(imm) >> (bits))))` which validates an (N+1)-bit signed range instead of the actual N-bit signed range. For example, `check_imm19(imm)` should validate a 19-bit signed range [-2^18, 2^18-1], but instead it checks for a 20-bit range by right-shifting by 19 bits. This allows out-of-range immediates to pass validation. The macro is used at lines 420 (check_imm26 for BPF_JA), 437 (check_imm19 for conditional jumps), 475 (check_imm26 for BPF_EXIT), and 545 (check_imm19 for CBZ). The vulnerable construct is present and unfixed in this initial commit.
